text:
mira: Heads-up — running into duplicate resource creates from the async Python client when requests timeout and then replay. Seen on prod after we bumped to 1.4.1.

sam: can you paste a minimal repro / logs? sounds like an idempotency replay bug not honoring the key? :eyes:

mira: short logs:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z INFO request start id=abc123 endpoint=/v1/resources
2026-03-18T09:12:05Z WARN request timeout id=abc123 elapsed=2.0s
2026-03-18T09:12:05Z INFO retrying request id=abc123 attempt=2 backoff=0.2s
2026-03-18T09:12:05Z INFO request start id=abc123 endpoint=/v1/resources
2026-03-18T09:12:06Z INFO 201 Created resource_id=rid_456
```
The server returned a 201 on the second attempt, so it looks like the first actually completed but the client timed out, retried, and then the app ended up with two creates (the service did not dedupe).

lucy: do you set X-Idempotency-Key header? which HTTP client?

mira: yes — we send X-Idempotency-Key. using httpx AsyncClient with timeout=2.0 and our own retry middleware in the SDK. header present: `X-Idempotency-Key: infra-20260318-abc123`.

mike: hmm. two possibilities i can think of:
1) the SDK retry middleware is re-sending without preserving the idempotency header (unlikely if header logged) or
2) the retry backoff jitter is tiny and all replicas/clients retry in-sync causing server to treat them as separate requests because it derives idempotency from more than just header (e.g. per-connection metadata).

mira: i dug deeper. the header is preserved. also only our single client produced the duplicates. i think the root cause is the combination of short timeout + our backoff implementation — we do `backoff = base * attempt + random()*jitter` which ends up with nearly identical intervals across attempts; at high load the server processes the request from attempt 1 late, attempt 2 reaches a different instance and creates new resource.

sam: sounds plausible. suggestion: switch to decorrelated jitter (aka exponential backoff with full jitter or "decorrelated jitter" from AWS blog) and make the async client cancel the in-flight connection more forcefully on timeout so we reduce overlapping in-flight requests.

mike: +1 on decorrelated jitter. also we should ensure replays include the exact same idempotency metadata (headers + body checksum) when sending to different backends. Servers sometimes use body checksum as part of the dedupe key.

mira: put together a tiny proposed patch for the py SDK retryer:
```
# pseudocode for Decorrelated Jitter
sleep = base
for attempt in range(1, max_attempts):
    sleep = min(cap, random_between(base, sleep * 3))
    await asyncio.sleep(sleep)
    do_request()
```
This avoids synchronized retries and caps the max backoff.

lucy: can you also add a test that simulates a delayed 201 (server responds after client timeout) and ensure only one create call reaches the server stub? We should add an integration-style test with an httpx mock.

mira: yes will add tests. question: should the SDK treat a client-side timeout as a definite failure and NOT retry automatically for non-idempotent endpoints (e.g., POST /resources) unless user explicitly opts in? Right now we retry some 5xx/timeouts by default.

sam: i think default should be conservative: automatic retries for safe/idempotent operations only. For POST-like endpoints we should honor the presence of a valid X-Idempotency-Key and only retry when that header is present and the server returned a 5xx or connection error. For timeouts, treat as transient but only replay if idempotency key was provided and user didn't opt-out. Document this clearly in the SDK docs.

mike: also add an SDK config flag `replay_on_timeout` that defaults to false for non-idempotent operations, true if idempotency header present. And expose a small async cancel helper that calls `client.aclose()` or cancels the request scope to avoid the race.

mira: filed issue and PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/py-sdk/pulls/789 (wip) — includes decorrelated jitter impl + tests + a new `replay_on_timeout` flag and docs updates. CI currently failing on one flaky test (timing-sensitive).

ci-bot: build #4521 failed — flaky test retry scheduled.

sam: nice. for the PR please include a small note in CHANGELOG and an entry in the troubleshooting docs about short timeouts + replays causing duplicate creates. also add an example snippet showing how to set `replay_on_timeout=True` with idempotency header.

mira: example snippet for docs:
```
from redwood import AsyncClient
async with AsyncClient(timeout=5.0, replay_on_timeout=False) as c:
    headers = {"X-Idempotency-Key": "user-123-req-1"}
    await c.post('/v1/resources', json={...}, headers=headers)
```

sam: ok, assigning to eng-sdk for review. I'll label P2 and add to next sprint. Thanks for the detailed repro, mira. :thumbsup:

mira: cool, i'll push the test fix and ping y'all when CI is green.

lucy: this is a good find — might save a lot of subtle production dupes.

mike: +1. we should also audit other SDKs for the same pattern (node/ruby) and make sure behavior is consistent across languages.

mira: filing follow-up cross-sdk audit ticket.

sam: closing loop here — triage done, PR in progress, docs + changelog noted.
